summary:
Project Summary – Galaxy Guardians: AI Space Scout 🚀

Our team, Galaxy Guardians, developed AI Space Scout, a project that helps identify the best places on Earth for astronauts to train before exploring the Moon and Mars.

We researched five locations: Antarctica, Iceland, Hawaii, the Atacama Desert, and Death Valley. Each location has special features that are similar to conditions on the Moon or Mars.

We designed a scoring system that compares these places based on rocks and soil, water and ice, environmental conditions, shelter possibilities, and scientific research value. Our AI-supported concept then recommends the best location for different missions, such as finding water, testing rovers, building habitats, or searching for signs of life.

Why is this important? - Astronauts need to prepare for the challenges of living and working in space. Our project shows how science, data, and AI can help scientists choose suitable training locations and make future space missions safer and more successful.
details:
Our project, AI Space Scout, helps scientists and astronauts find suitable places on Earth to prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars.

We researched five locations: Antarctica, Iceland, Hawaii, the Atacama Desert, and Death Valley. Each location has special features that resemble conditions astronauts might experience in space.

We created an Analog Finder scoring system that compares these locations using five factors: rocks and soil, water and ice, environmental conditions, shelter possibilities, and scientific research value. Each factor has a different weight, helping us calculate scores and identify suitable locations for different missions.

Our project can help astronauts prepare for challenges such as finding water, testing rovers, building habitats, and searching for life. It could make future space exploration safer and better planned.

We used online research, scientific information, and presentation software to develop and demonstrate our concept. Our AI-supported recommendation system is currently a prototype idea rather than a fully developed application.

What makes our project creative is that we don't simply choose one best location. We recommend different places depending on the mission's purpose.

Our goal is to show how young scientists can use research, technology, and creative thinking to support future space exploration.
